transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

[Heading: Probably normal induction hum]
That is very likely to be perfectly normal. Induction hobs work by creating a magnetic field that makes the base of your pan vibrate at high frequency; this often causes a buzzing or humming sound, especially with heavy, multi-layered stockpots on high power settings. It is not about to break unless you hear loud cracking, see sparks, smell burning plastic, or if the hob switches off with an error code. To be sure it’s just the pan resonating, try placing a flat hand lightly on the side of the pot (switched off first) – if the noise changes or stops when you touch it, that confirms it is mechanical vibration from the cookware. If the sound continues at low power settings, or if there are any warning signs like burning smells or error codes, then please let me know and we can look further.

Thanks. It does get much quieter at power level 6 and below. No error codes and no burning smell, and the hob hasn't cut out. I'm not sure how to do the hand test, because the buzzing only happens when the zone is on high. Is it likely just this pot?

[Heading: Normal induction pan resonance]
That confirms it is normal behaviour. The noise you are hearing is called 'coil whine' or pan resonance: the magnetic field makes the metal base of your stockpot vibrate at a high frequency, which creates that buzzing sound. It is very common with large, heavy pots on high power settings and is not a sign that the hob is about to break. The fact that it gets much quieter at lower power levels (6 and below) is exactly what you would expect, as the magnetic field strength—and thus the vibration—is reduced. Since there are no error codes, no burning smells, and the hob hasn't cut out, your appliance is functioning correctly. If you find the noise too distracting in future, it usually helps to ensure the pot base is perfectly flat and clean (any warping or debris can increase vibration), or to use a slightly smaller pot if available. Otherwise, you can continue using it with confidence.
